briefing.summary: Strong bullish reversal day. After a brutal -2.1% selloff on Jan 20 triggered by Trump's Greenland tariff threats against 8 European nations, the setup for Jan 21 is a classic relief rally. Trump speaks at Davos WEF at ~1pm ET and by ~2:30pm ET announces he's reached a 'framework deal' with NATO's Rutte on Greenland, pausing all threatened tariffs on European nations. Markets were 'still sinking' in the morning on tariff fears, then staged a massive afternoon reversal. The Dow closed +588pts (+1.2%), S&P 500 +1.16% to 6,875.62, Nasdaq +1.18%. This is a textbook 'buy the dip after geopolitical scare' setup, amplified by oversold conditions from the prior day's sharp decline.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: DOMINANT CATALYST: Trump announced Jan 17 that 8 European nations (Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, UK) face 10% tariffs Feb 1 (escalating to 25% June 1) unless Greenland is sold. This triggered the Jan 20 selloff (-2.1% on S&P). On Jan 21 at Davos, Trump first said he 'won't use force' for Greenland, then at ~2:30pm ET posted he reached a 'framework deal' with NATO Secretary General Rutte, pausing all European tariffs. Markets surged on relief. Greenland crisis Wikipedia shows Denmark committed $13.7B to Arctic defense. Separately, the Supreme Court IEEPA tariff challenge was pending (ruled Feb 20 that IEEPA tariffs unconstitutional 6-3). Ken Griffin at Davos warned trade policy uncertainty is weighing on global investment decisions.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Fed funds rate at 3.50-3.75% after three consecutive 25bp cuts. Next FOMC meeting Jan 27-28 expected to hold steady (confirmed: held). Two dissenting members (Miran, Waller) preferred another 25bp cut. 10-year Treasury yield around 4.1-4.2%. Gold rallied 9% in January on geopolitical uncertainty, GLD went from $421.29 (Jan 16) to $437.23 (Jan 20) to $443.60 (Jan 21). WTI crude below $60, weak. IMF raised China 2026 growth forecast to 4.5% on US trade truce. Chief Economists at Davos discussed AI productivity boost of 0.1-0.8% to global GDP.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: KEY EARNINGS JAN 21: Johnson & Johnson reported Q4 before market open - beat with $2.46 adj EPS, revenue $24.6B (+9.1%). 2026 guidance above consensus at $99.5-100.5B revenue. Stock relatively flat at $218.21 (from $218.66). Netflix reported Jan 20 after close - beat EPS ($0.56 vs $0.55) and revenue ($12.05B vs $11.97B), 325M subscribers, but 2026 guidance disappointed (11-13% growth slowdown). NFLX dropped from $87.26 to $85.36 (-2.2%). 3M reported Jan 20 - beat EPS $1.83 vs $1.81, but stock dropped hard from $167.80 to $155.88 (-7.1%) on Jan 21. Ericsson reported strong Q4 with 6% organic growth and SEK 25B shareholder distribution plan, stock surged ~11%. Procter & Gamble earnings due Jan 22 (beat). Intel earnings due Jan 22 after close.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: AI infrastructure spending remains the dominant investment theme. Nvidia has $275B backlog, expected $65B Q4 revenue. Chinese companies ordered 2M+ H200 chips potentially worth $40B. AMD surged 7.7% on Jan 21 ($231.83 to $249.80) on Turin server CPU demand - nearly sold out for 2026, potential 15% price hikes. Bernstein upgraded AMD server forecast to 30% growth. Intel surged 11% ($48.56 to $54.25) on server CPU demand + upcoming earnings. Davos attendees expressed concerns about AI bubble but acknowledged 0.1-0.8% GDP boost potential. Broadcom fell from $351.71 to $332.60 on Jan 21 despite broad market rally - unusual weakness.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: WTI crude below $60, testing resistance near $62. Kazakhstan halted Tengiz/Korolev oil production temporarily due to power issues. Trump at Davos highlighted US natural gas production at all-time highs, oil production up 730K bpd. XLE flat ($47.69 to $47.60 on Jan 21). Energy is not a catalyst here - sidelined by low prices and oversupply narrative. Trump executive order banning large institutional investors from buying single-family homes was a Davos announcement.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Trump's Davos speech covered: (1) Greenland framework deal/tariff pause - biggest market mover. (2) 'Won't use force' for Greenland - de-escalation. (3) Executive order banning institutional investors from buying single-family homes. (4) Claims of 1.6% core inflation and 5.4% Q4 GDP growth. (5) Iran tariff threats: 25% on any country doing business with Iran, 'effective immediately.' Supreme Court IEEPA tariff case pending - would ultimately rule tariffs unconstitutional on Feb 20. NATO Golden Dome missile defense initiative projected at $1.1T.

recommendations.thesis: AMD demonstrated remarkable relative strength by holding $231.83 through the Jan 20 selloff while the S&P dropped 2.1%. The Turin CPU demand catalyst is company-specific and powerful - being sold out for a full year with pricing power is rare. The tariff relief rally provides a macro tailwind on top of the fundamental catalyst. This is a convergence trade: strong idiosyncratic catalyst + macro relief + technical resilience.
recommendations.catalyst: Turin server CPU demand explosion - AMD nearly sold out for 2026 with potential 15% price hikes. Bernstein upgraded server business forecast to 30% growth. Broader tariff relief rally provides tailwind. Stock held flat through Jan 20 selloff (unusual relative strength) signaling strong bid.

recommendations.thesis: Intel is in the midst of a multi-catalyst setup: server CPU demand sold out (matching AMD narrative), analyst upgrades, pre-earnings momentum, and the broader tariff relief rally. The stock has been re-rated from turnaround story to growth story. The 140% gain in the past year shows strong institutional momentum. Pre-earnings runs into strong results can be powerful.
recommendations.catalyst: Intel surging on server CPU demand + KeyBanc upgrade. Stock up 140% in past year. Earnings due Jan 22 after close creating pre-earnings momentum bid. Sold-out server CPU supply for 2026 mirrors AMD's demand surge. US government + Nvidia investment backstops foundry story.

recommendations.thesis: This is the highest-probability trade on the board. The Jan 20 selloff was driven by a specific, identifiable geopolitical catalyst (Greenland tariffs) that gets resolved on Jan 21. The Baird report noted investor positioning was extremely bullish going into the selloff, meaning the selloff was more about positioning unwind than fundamental deterioration. Once the tariff threat is removed, the dip-buyers return aggressively. The S&P was only 2.6% from all-time highs.
recommendations.catalyst: Classic relief rally setup. S&P 500 fell 2.1% on Jan 20 (worst day since Oct 2025) on Greenland tariff threat. Trump scheduled to speak at Davos Jan 21, and by 2:30pm ET announces framework deal pausing all European tariffs. Market was only 2.6% below all-time high from Jan 12 - this is a dip in an uptrend, not a breakdown.

recommendations.thesis: Netflix is a rare short opportunity on a broadly bullish day. When a stock can't rally with the market after reporting earnings, it signals that sellers are in control. The 2026 guidance showing 11-13% growth is a meaningful deceleration that re-rates the multiple lower. The stock declining while the Dow surges 580 points is a powerful negative divergence. Fund managers who were overweight will need to reduce positions.
recommendations.catalyst: Q4 earnings beat was overshadowed by disappointing 2026 guidance (11-13% revenue growth slowdown from 16-18%). Market expected acceleration but got deceleration. Analyst price targets cut 8.2%. Stock hit 52-week low. Shares fell despite overall market rally on Jan 21 - relative weakness signals distribution.

recommendations.thesis: Tesla is a high-beta play on the tariff relief rally. The stock dropped more than the broader market on Jan 20, creating room for an outsized bounce. European tariff removal is directly relevant given Tesla's significant European manufacturing (Giga Berlin) and sales exposure. Tesla trades as a sentiment/momentum vehicle, and the shift from fear to relief is its optimal environment.
recommendations.catalyst: Tesla dropped 4.2% on Jan 20 in the tariff-driven selloff, creating a dip-buy opportunity. European tariff relief directly benefits Tesla's European operations and removes a risk overhang. Risk-on rotation supports high-beta names. Trump's pro-business Davos speech positive for Musk-adjacent names.
